sources.title: NGSS 4-ESS1-1: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time
Geological Society of London: Burial and Compaction (oldest layers at the bottom)
National Park Service, Grand Teton: Fossils (marine fossils show an ancient sea floor)
National Park Service, Grand Canyon: Fossils

steps.title: Cliff
steps.instruction: Trace the side of the cliff.

note.text: A cliff or canyon wall shows rock layers, one on top of another, like a stack of pancakes.

steps.title: Layers
steps.instruction: Draw the lines between the four layers.

note.text: Layers form as mud and sand settle in flat sheets, one on top of the last. So the bottom layer is the oldest; the top is the youngest.

steps.title: Shells
steps.instruction: Trace the three shell fossils in the bottom layer.

note.text: These are fossils of sea animals. Finding them tells us this place was once the floor of a sea.
note.remember: Sea fossils: there was once a sea.

steps.title: Fish
steps.instruction: Trace the fish fossil and its tail in the second layer.

note.text: A fish fossil means water was still here when this layer formed, after the bottom layer.
Hard parts like bones and shells are what usually turn into fossils.

steps.title: Fern
steps.instruction: Draw the fern fossil in the top layer: its stem and leaves.

note.text: Ferns grow on land. A land plant in the top layer shows that, much later, the sea was gone and land took its place.
note.remember: Fossils show how a place changed.

options.feedback: Yes. Each layer settled on top of the one before, so the bottom layer is the oldest.
The top layer settled last, so it's the youngest. The bottom one is oldest.
Layers form one at a time, each on top of the last.
The fern is in the top layer, the youngest. The bottom layer formed first.

steps.title: Explain the change
steps.question: What do the fossils tell us about how this place changed over time?

options.text: It was once covered by water, and later became land
options.feedback: Right. Sea fossils at the bottom, a fish above, then a land fern on top: the water went away over a very long time.
Shell and fish fossils show there was once water here.

options.text: It started as land and became a sea
options.feedback: Read from the bottom up: sea fossils come first (oldest), the land fern last.
Fossils are evidence: they show what lived here, and so what the place was like.
